passage_title: A Better Note in the Margin
student_passage:
A Better Note in the Margin

The first batch of rolls emerged from the oven pale and dense, Mina stared at the tray while the kitchen filled with the smell of warm cardamom.[1] She had promised to bring her grandmother's rolls to the neighborhood breakfast, and the penciled recipe had never failed before.

Mina reread the card and noticed that its instruction to add 'one cup' did not identify how tightly the flour should be packed.[2] Instead of immediately adding more yeast, she weighed a loosely filled cup and a firmly packed one. The second held far more flour, enough to make the dough stubborn[3] and dry.

Mina mixed another batch with the lighter measure. On the other hand,[4] the new dough stretched easily beneath her fingers and rose above the rim of the bowl. The baked rolls separated into soft layers.

Before leaving, Mina added a sentence to the recipe card: spoon the flour into the cup, then level it. The note was small, but they[5] preserved the discovery that had saved the morning.
